completeness.exhaustion: Each criterion is an explicit exhaustive classification at the registered boundary. Their generated product contains every same-grammar coordinate form and does not select a neighborhood around the survivor.

closure.coordinate: The held count identifies how many equal disjoint fibres are selected; the whole count identifies the complete equal-fibre partition.
closure.positive_boundary: The count dependency permits only generated nonempty finite traces. A within-partition selection cannot contain more fibres than its whole.
closure.minimality: Removing either count loses selection or reference identity; relaxing complete, disjoint, equal or contained status destroys exact part meaning; adding another coordinate is unforced.
closure.generality: The criterion product is unchanged for every generated positive finite whole count and every generated nonempty contained selection. No maximum depth, semantic zero or completed infinity is installed.
closure.unresolved: Whether two coordinates generated from different partitions represent the same part is not assumed here and requires a later common-refinement equivalence derivation.

completeness.pair_cell_rule: For every generated fibre label of A, generate one cell with every generated fibre label of B. The ordered pair label retains both origins.

closure.common_refinement: The nested pair-cell generator is finite whenever both source traces are generated finite traces. Grouping cells by their first label refines A; grouping by their second label refines B. No multiplication law is assumed.
closure.equivalence: Lift each held selection to all pair cells descending from its held source fibres. The coordinates identify the same exact part precisely when the two lifted selected traces admit a complete one-to-one and onto pairing.
closure.reflexive: The generated identity pairing relates every lifted trace to itself.
closure.symmetric: Reversing every pair in a bijection yields a bijection in the other direction.
closure.transitive: Chaining the unique mates through two bijections yields one mate in the composite pairing.
closure.refinement_invariance: Uniformly refining every cell appends the same complete finite descendant trace on both sides, so pairing existence is preserved.
closure.minimality: Removing either refinement, either complete lift, or either direction of pairing leaves the equality witness incomplete; extra scale data is unforced.
closure.named_shape_uniqueness: Only complete__disjoint__equal__a-refined__b-refined__a-selection-complete__b-selection-complete__bijective__no-extra is a complete parameter-free witness.
closure.generality: The pair-cell and pairing construction applies to every two generated positive finite partition traces and is independent of a maximum depth.

completeness.exhaustion: The positive-count dependency classifies a transformation as no extension, its first extension or any later extension. Every other criterion is an explicit exhaustive relation at the declared boundary; their product generates all same-grammar forms.

closure.minimal_count: The structural One is the identity base. Appending one generated occurrence is the first nonidentity positive count. Every later finite extension contains this earlier nontrivial stage and is therefore not minimal.
closure.equal_fibres: The unqualified One supplies no selector that can privilege one fibre. An unequal allocation therefore requires additional data, while equal fibre status does not.
closure.held_labels: Nontrivial distinction requires different exact labels. They are held structural identities, not positive and negative numerical quantities.
closure.return: Complete disjoint fibres retain the One only when their complete assembly has an explicit return relation to the source whole.
closure.minimality: Identity is trivial; later extensions are overbuilt; removing equality, disjointness, distinct held labels or return loses a Fold requirement; adding data violates parameter freedom.
closure.generality: First-extension minimality follows from the base/successor count structure at every later generated finite depth; it does not depend on a maximum census depth or completed infinity.

completeness.recursion: Begin with the structural empty One word. At each generated Fold successor, append held-a and held-b once to every prior word.

closure.base: The empty One word is the complete support before a Fold; empty is a structural form, not numerical zero.
closure.successor: Appending each of the two distinct held labels once to every prior word produces all and only the next support.
closure.uniqueness: Distinct prior words or distinct appended held labels yield distinct successor traces.
closure.return: The return relation at each Fold node reunites its two successor branches to their predecessor whole.
closure.minimality: Removing a word loses support; duplicating or adding a word is nonminimal; missing transitions or returns loses construction identity.
closure.generality: The base and successor clauses apply to every generated finite Fold depth without a maximum or completed infinity.

controls.expected: reject incomplete one-step support
controls.observed: a single held-label word omits the other forced branch

controls.expected: reject changed source identity
controls.observed: changed identity differs

controls.expected: reject duplicated or missing word support
controls.observed: generated depths one through five are unique, equal-length and complete

controls.expected: refuse imported binary numerals, exponentiation and completed-infinite support
controls.observed: support is generated only by finite held-label recursion

closure.cast: For positive n/d, repeated removal acts only while n/d exceeds the One; termination leaves an exact part in (0, One], and an exact whole terminates at the One.
closure.fold: For an admitted part x, x joined to itself lies in (0, two Ones]; casting therefore returns exactly one admitted part.
closure.take: For admitted a>b, the guarded difference is strictly positive and smaller than the One.
closure.unison: The positive relation a/a is exactly the One; coincidence is identity, not a numerical zero.
closure.exactness: Integer pairs reduce through the host Fraction carrier; no decimal, irrational or imaginary proof value is constructible.
closure.minimality: Removing a guard, cast convention, closure, unison or trace loses a required invariant; adding an operation is unforced.
closure.generality: The numerator/denominator arguments apply to every admitted finite positive count pair, not a chosen denominator bound.

selection_classes: one held fibre modulo held-label exchange

closure.forced_coordinate: The first Fold has exactly two equal fibres. Any one held fibre therefore has coordinate one-of-two; label exchange changes the held identity but not the exact part coordinate.
closure.uniqueness: If an exact positive part x joins with itself to the One, its selected count must equal its unselected count in the two-fibre refinement; both are the singleton equivalence class.
closure.complement: The other singleton fibre is the complement of the held singleton and has the same one-of-two coordinate, so half-One is self-complementary in exact part value.
closure.fold: Self-junction of the singleton equivalence class completes both fibres; casting that complete turn is the One.
closure.fixed_one: Self-junction of the One makes two complete Ones and cast removes one complete One, retaining the One.
closure.terminology: Complement sends x to the remainder within the One. Phase antipode translates x by half-One and casts. They are separately named operations; at half-One the phase antipode is the One, while the complement has half-One value.
closure.minimality: Whole selection is not a proper ground; any unequal or additional selection violates the minimal equal two-fibre Fold.
closure.generality: The equivalence argument uses the complete first-Fold partition, not a sampled rational search.

closure.domain: For x in (0, One], self-junction lies in (0, two Ones]; exact cast returns (0, One].
closure.preimages: For image y, the lower preimage y/2 and upper preimage cast(y/2 plus half-One) are distinct, lie on opposite half-circles and both Fold to y. Any Fold preimage has one of these two forms.
closure.phase_antipode: Adding half-One twice adds one complete One, which cast removes; therefore phase antipode is an involution. Doubling a half-One translation adds one complete One before cast, so both phase partners share one Fold image.
closure.uniform_partition: For an even generated count two-n, images of i/(two-n) identify i with i+n and are exactly j/n for the n positive residue classes; their distinct sorted gaps remain one/n.
closure.first_cycle: Fold sends one-of-three to two-of-three and two-of-three back to one-of-three. No nonstatic cycle can have positive length below the first count extension beyond identity.
closure.minimality: Deleting either preimage, cast closure, phase relation, uniform image or return loses an exact Fold invariant; extra dynamics are unforced.
closure.generality: The proofs use arbitrary positive numerator/denominator and arbitrary generated positive n, not the finite controls below.

closure.primitive_exhaustion: At normalized primitive cost through two source occurrences, total parameter-free self-map expressions reduce operationally to x, x-times-x, the One, or cast(x joined x); raw junction is not total, guarded removal is not total, multiplication by One is identity and closed whole expressions cast to One.
closure.behavior: Identity is static; square sends every proper x to a strictly smaller positive x-squared; constant-One collapses; Fold has two preimages for each image and the exact two-cycle one-third/two-thirds.
closure.least_size: Fold qualifies at size one. Every ordered word of size greater than one is later by positive construction count and therefore cannot be a least-size generator.
closure.composition_induction: Appending one primitive to a generated word increases its positive construction size; induction excludes all sizes beyond the executed three from displacing the size-one survivor.
closure.conditional_scope: Uniqueness is claimed only for the declared normalized parameter-free self-map and ordered-composition grammar with generation defined as noninjective plus nonstatic recurrence.
closure.minimality: Removing Fold loses the only generating primitive; admitting a larger word violates least-size selection; adding a literal or primitive changes the grammar and is outside the theorem.
closure.generality: The positive-size successor excludes every finite later composition, not only the 84 executed prefix forms.
